learningObjective: Separate the global state and joint actions available to a centralized learner during training from the local observation available to each policy during decentralized execution.
mediumRationale: A deterministic SVG is the smallest medium that can align two agents, distinguish action paths from training-only update paths, and place a hard divider between training and execution. Fixed geometry keeps the privileged-information boundary explicit without requiring interaction.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: a flowchart could show connectivity, but reliably aligning two actor lanes above an execution boundary while distinguishing training-only feedback would require more layout complexity than the concept warrants.
mediumComparison.svg: Selected: a compact, deterministic two-phase schematic directly aligns each local observation, policy, and action while using labeled solid and dashed paths to expose the training-only critic.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected: a table could list which inputs are available, but it would not make the joint critic input and the disappearance of its feedback path spatially traceable.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: toggling between train and deploy would hide one state at a time and add controls without improving the side-by-side comparison.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: MADDPG and QMIX figures are method-specific and denser than this article needs; permissive reuse permission was not established for the candidate paper artwork.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: prose names centralized training and decentralized execution but does not make it immediately apparent which information crosses into policy decisions and which exists only to shape training.

pages.insight: The preceding page concludes model explainability with a SHAP example and contains no reinforcement-learning or multi-agent mechanism.
This is the deck's Reinforcement Learning section divider and contains no technical figure.
The ML-versus-RL slide contrasts iid supervised samples with dependent trajectories and describes learning a state-to-action mapping, but it discusses only the single-agent setting.

The policy-optimization slide presents a single CartPole policy network, sampled action, reward trajectory, and policy-gradient update; it has no other agents, centralized critic, or train/deploy information boundary.
The following page begins Past projects, confirming the local RL section ends without a multi-agent treatment.

deckReview.notes: GitHub Copilot CLI agent-6 text-indexed all 214 pages of the local PDF for multi-agent, reinforcement learning, MADDPG, QMIX, centralized, and decentralized terms, then inspected pages 153-157 individually. Only pages 154-156 concern RL, and they cover section context, ML-versus-RL, and a single-agent policy-gradient example. No slide depicts multi-agent learning or CTDE, so no deck figure applies and no deck artwork is reused.

sources.title: Multi-Agent Actor-Critic for Mixed Cooperative-Competitive Environments
sources.usage: Used to verify the MADDPG pattern: decentralized actors use local observations while a centralized critic can use all agents' actions and additional state information during training.
sources.license: The paper is publicly readable on arXiv, but permissive figure-reuse permission was not established. No figure, geometry, prose, data, or artwork was copied or adapted.

sources.title: QMIX: Monotonic Value Function Factorisation for Deep Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
sources.usage: Used to verify the broader CTDE distinction: centralized learning may condition on extra state while the learned per-agent values and resulting policies remain decentralized.
sources.license: The PMLR paper is publicly accessible, but no paper figure is reused. The article's actor-critic schematic is independently composed and does not reproduce QMIX's mixing-network architecture.

sources.license: This official licensing guidance is cited only to determine reuse treatment; no text or visual asset is reproduced.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest mental model in the article is the asymmetry in CTDE: privileged global information can influence parameter learning without becoming an input to deployed decisions. The shipped SVG is an original abstraction rather than a redraw of a paper architecture. It makes no empirical claim and uses the primary papers only to check the information paths.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, indexed the complete 214-page deck and inspected the full neighboring RL section, then checked the primary MADDPG and QMIX papers plus official arXiv licensing guidance before selecting an original CTDE information-boundary schematic.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a programmatic title and detailed description. Every observation, policy, action, critic input, and phase is directly labeled; solid forward paths, dashed learning paths, and a ruled train/execution divider preserve the lesson without color. The established visual-wide and visual-scroll primitives keep a readable fixed label size through intentional horizontal scrolling at 390 CSS pixels, theme variables provide light and dark contrast, and existing print overrides provide a light high-contrast rendering.
